about: Characterization of today's outputs, not a requirement. A difference means the output changed: regenerate with T2_CHARACTERIZATION_WRITE=1 and review the change. The anomaly family's strings are left out.
description: Strongest spectral line at 2x shaft speed, catalog bearing 6205

diagnose_vibration.overall_diagnosis: ISO Severity: Zone A (Good) — RMS velocity 1.00 mm/s. Dominant frequency: 60.0 Hz (shaft: 29.9 Hz). The strongest line of the spectrum is at 2.00 times the declared shaft frequency (within 5 % of 2x). Its dominance does not identify a fault, and it is not counted as a finding. This check cannot distinguish the 2x response of a machine in normal condition from misalignment, mechanical looseness, a rub, a shaft crack, a shaft or rotor with asymmetric stiffness, a resonance near twice running speed, the passing tone of a rotor with two blades or lobes, vibration transmitted from another machine, a component at the electrical supply frequency, which lies close to 2x on a four-pole motor, or, on a two-pole motor, the electromagnetic vibration at twice the supply frequency, which lies close to 2x (exactly at 2x on a synchronous motor). Narrowing these down needs more than this check, such as a finer analysis of the line's frequency, a baseline from the same machine at the same condition, phase, a second radial or an axial channel, or several speeds. Establishing a cause needs a physical check of the machine. Another analysis that reads this same line of the same signal repeats the observation and does not corroborate it. Bearing analysis: No eligible line at a tested characteristic frequency stands above the local noise floor in this record and band. This is not evidence that the bearing is free of defects. Combined evidence across the analyses that ran: none. It counts findings, is not a probability, and does not identify or confirm a fault type.
recommendations: Continue routine monitoring per maintenance schedule.

The inner-race line (BPFI) does not stand above the local noise floor in this record and band. The rolling-element line (2 x BSF) does not stand above the local noise floor in this record and band. The cage line (FTF) does not stand above the local noise floor in this record and band.

The largest share of STFT energy is in the 0-100 Hz band (100% of the total). This percentage describes the measured signal and does not identify a fault. The relative distribution across frequency bands can change with the measured physical quantity (for example, acceleration versus velocity).

No healthy baseline was supplied for this machine, so the readings below are absolute rather than relative. Whether this condition is new, stable, or worsening cannot be determined from a single acquisition.
Dominant frequency in the raw spectrum: 60.0 Hz.

Envelope spectrum with the FTF, BPFO, BSF and BPFI search windows overlaid. Each shaded band is the ±5% window around the line its check tests (2 x BSF for the rolling element). A peak inside a window is not a finding by itself: the check counts a line only when it stands above the local noise floor and a further line it predicts does too. No window is emphasised: the bearing statement in this report names no candidate line.
